title: Swarm Exposure
one_liner: Stack hundreds of simulated night-sky frames and watch satellite trails pile up into a glowing band.
speaker: Salim Ismail
context: A New Zealand photographer stacked hundreds of frames over Mount Taranaki and captured thousands of satellite trails. Alex calls it a baby Dyson swarm and predicts a visible compute halo in sun-synchronous orbit.
demo: The visitor sees a dark sky over a mountain silhouette and presses 'Expose'. Frames stack one by one and the trails build up into a band with a running count of frames, satellites and trails. A 'future' slider adds more satellites, including a sun-synchronous ring, so the visitor can watch the band turn into a halo at dusk.
data_plan: Simulated orbits rendered on a canvas, clearly labelled. The episode's photo figures (578 frames, ~1,400 satellites, ~15,000 trail appearances) are used as the default 'today' preset.
risks: Orbits are simplified, not real satellite data. It must be labelled as an illustration, not a forecast of brightness.
